final_text:
Of the 10 organisms added to spike_P0, 5 were detected and 5 were missed. I read the species-level (rank code S) clade read counts straight from `data/spike_P0.report.gz`.

| Organism (manifest) | Pairs added | Species clade reads | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pseudomonas aeruginosa | 40,000 | 811 | detected |
| Enterococcus faecalis | 40,000 | 6,457 | detected |
| Escherichia coli | 4,000 | 72 | detected |
| Staphylococcus aureus | 4,000 | 54 | detected |
| Lactobacillus fermentum (listed as Limosilactobacillus fermentum in the report) | 40 | 26 | detected |
| Salmonella enterica | 400 | 4 | missed (below 10) |
| Bacillus subtilis | 40 | 2 | missed (below 10) |
| Listeria monocytogenes | 400 | no species row | missed |
| Saccharomyces cerevisiae | 40,000 | not in the report | missed |
| Cryptococcus neoformans | 4,000 | not in the report | missed |

- **Listeria:** the report has 315 reads assigned only at genus level (*Listeria*, taxid 1637). There is no species row, so under your rule it counts as missed.
- **The two yeasts:** no Saccharomyces or Cryptococcus row appears anywhere in the report. Eukaryota (3,117,739 reads) has no fungal entries under it. The database used for classification probably has no fungal genomes, but the report alone can't confirm that.
- **Low recovery overall:** even the detected organisms come back at a small fraction of what was added. For example, *P. aeruginosa* got 811 reads out of 40,000 pairs.
